title: dispatcher: forbid handoffs in .agent/repo=.this; a handoff lives in its route
description:
## .what

a rule for the dispatcher role: **forbid handoffs in `.agent/repo=.this/`.** a handoff lives in the
route that raised it: `.behavior/<route>/handoff.<owner>.<subject>.md`.

## .why

- a handoff is temporary: a live ask of another owner, moot the day that owner lands it.
  `.agent/repo=.this/` holds what stays true (rules, howtos, terms, invariants)
- the route raised the ask, holds its evidence, and closes with it. outside the route the ask
  outlives its context and reads as settled doctrine
- every brief under `.agent/repo=.this/` costs a boot path line every session, so a stale ask
  taxes every reader

## .the test

> will this file be wrong, or moot, once another owner acts? yes → a handoff; it goes in the route

## .enforcement

- a `handoff.*` under `.agent/repo=.this/` = blocker; move it to the route that raised it
- a durable brief that cites a route handoff as ground for a durable claim = blocker; state the
  durable fact in its own words

## .measured

uladkasach/dev-env-setup, 2026-11-22: a driver wrote an infra handoff into
`.agent/repo=.this/role=any/briefs/grove/backup/`, then listed it under boot `not` to fit the
budget. the human ruled it belongs in the route. a second, older handoff sat in `briefs/creds/`
the same way. both moved; the repo carries `rule.forbid.handoffs-in-agent-repo-this` locally.

## .ask

add `rule.forbid.handoffs-in-agent-repo-this` to the dispatcher role's briefs, say-level and
short, so every repo that enrolls the dispatcher inherits it. a dispatch skill that writes a
handoff should default its path to the bound route.
